detail: defence secalign: the thesis cites SecAlign and serves it as a LoRA adapter on Llama 3.1 8B; which released adapter was used is not stated
report: Gemini was run once per case, the other models three times; quantised weights for the 32B and 70B models; spotlighting raises InjecAgent attack success on Llama 3.1 8B (0.862 to 0.922)

report: 100 queries per dataset; the defence changes the prompt's exemplars as well as adding the reasoning line, so the reference arm is the paper's standard four-exemplar prompt (instruction_prompt_only)

defences ig_*: IntentGuard's trust labels come from the agent's message segments (tool responses untrusted), which is coded as chat roles; the masking step uses the model's own listed intent, not a separate classifier, which is why it is kept under amendment 4
report: each attack is optimised separately against each defence and the undefended model, so attacker matching is by procedure and budget, not by identical injections

comparisons: the only reference is GPT-3.5-Turbo fine-tuned on the same summaries, a different and far larger base, so every comparison has an unmatched base; whether the 72 HOUYI prompts were the same for every model is not stated; 13.80% does not correspond to a whole number of 72 prompts

claim k1: the 94.7% figure is for the full system, which includes input sanitisation; the in-scope comparison is the ablation without the sanitiser, whose attack success is only given pooled over all six categories, including direct injection

report: the base model is described only as a 7B pre-trained model and the training and test data as collected from operational environments; which model the Instruction Hierarchy prompt runs on is not stated and is taken to be the same base

comparisons c_f4_*: Figure 4 is said to use the strongest attacker, but SafeReview's values there equal its Qwen3-4B row in Table 2, so the comparison uses that evaluation with the attacker marked matched_unstated; SecAlign's base and training data are not stated

report: attack success is not measured directly: FPR depends on a threshold calibrated per condition and the average rating mixes defence effect with review calibration; the GRPO attackers were trained against the undefended reviewer
report: distractors are plausible irrelevant instructions rather than attacks, so distractor execution is coded as a proxy for injection success; the GPT-5.4 mini defence rows are single runs

report: defences are measured on GPT-4o only; Figure 2 shows spotlighting's attack success rising with context length (about 32% at 1K tokens to 72% at 16K) without an undefended curve, so it is not coded

results r_f12_*: Figure 12 plots unlabelled points, so the values are not coded; read from the chart, indirect attack success is about 6.9% for GPT-5.3, 6.0% for GPT-5.4, 4.0% for GPT-5.5 and 3.8% for GPT-5.6

report: there is no undefended arm: every compared production model already had instruction-hierarchy training and, from GPT-5.2 on, attacks from GPT-Red precursors, and successive models differ in much more than this training; Figure 11 and the IPI 2025 result have no comparator; the training targets are not described beyond reward design
